title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Unified Onboarding, Quantization, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Priya Patel
content:
Overview:
This playbook describes Redwood's unified process for onboarding new models into the eval-harness, integrating quantization profiles, and the end-to-end regression triage workflow. It operationalizes responsibilities, SLOs, tooling, and escalation steps so model onboarding is predictable and regressions are diagnosed and remediated within defined SLAs.

Scope:
- Applies to all model onboarding (open-source and partner models) intended for serving on Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers: initial eval harness integration, prompt set standardization, quantization profile validation, continuous monitoring, and regression triage.

Goals:
1) Reduce time-to-production for verified model variants to <= 14 days from intake.
2) Detect and triage quality regressions within 24 hours of alert.
3) Maintain model acceptance gates: functional, safety, and quality thresholds.

Stakeholders and Ownership:
- Applied ML (owner): end-to-end onboarding, eval config, prompt set curation.
- Serving Runtime (support): integration validation, perf/latency profiling.
- SRE (support): monitoring, alerting, and incident response for eval infra.
- Product/Platform (reviewer): business requirements and rollout gating.

High-level process (Steps):
1) Intake and Triage (2 business days)
   - Submit Model Intake ticket using the Model Intake template (link to template).
   - Required artifacts: model weights URI, expected tokenizer, model card, intended use-cases, baseline prompt sets, recommended quantization configs.
   - Applied ML assigns a tracker and owner.

2) Eval Harness Integration (3-5 business days)
   - Create eval harness job: add model config to eval-harness repo: tests/<model-name>/config.yaml. Example config snippet:

     name: "my-candidate-model"
     weights_uri: "s3://redwood-models/my-candidate-model/v1"
     tokenizer: "sentencepiece"
     sequence_length: 2048
     expected_latency_ms: 60

   - Implement scoring adapters if model output format differs (see adapter examples in eval-harness/docs/adapters.md).
   - Run baseline benchmarks: throughput, token-per-second, cold-start latency, and memory.

3) Prompt-set Standardization (1-2 business days)
   - Curate canonical prompt sets by intent: summarization, instruction-following, code, classification. Follow naming convention: prompt-sets/<model-name>/<intent>-v1.jsonl.
   - Each prompt entry must include: id, input, reference, tags (e.g., safety, performance), and expected metric.
   - Minimum required prompt count per intent: 200 for general intents, 500 for high-risk (safety/legal/health).

4) Quantization Profile Validation (2-3 business days)
   - Apply recommended quantization profile(s) from quantization-profiles catalog.
   - Run automated regression-suite comparing fp16 baseline -> int8/4-bit profile across prompt sets.
   - Metrics to capture: EM (exact match), ROUGE-L, BLEU, embedding-similarity (cosine) and token-level perplexity delta.
   - Accept criteria: quality delta <= 3% relative drop on primary metric OR embedding cosine >= 0.98, and latency/cost improvement >= 1.7x.

5) Canary and Rollout Guidance (ongoing)
   - If model passes acceptance, schedule canary on Dedicated/Hosted with traffic=1-5% for 48-72 hours. Monitor automatically: quality metrics, latency P50/P95, error rate, and cost-per-token.
   - Rollout steps: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on regression alerts.

SLOs and Thresholds:
- Regression detection: alert if primary quality metric drops > 2% absolute or > 5% relative over 24h rolling window.
- Latency SLO: P95 inference latency < 300ms for short-form prompts (<128 tokens) on Hosted default instance types.
- Cost target: quantized variant should reduce tokens/second unit-cost by >= 30% versus baseline for production consideration.

Monitoring and Alerts:
- Eval-harness -> pushes summary metrics to Redwood Metrics (metric names: eval.quality.<model>.<intent>.<metric>).
- Alerts:
  1) quality-regression-high (SEV2): triggered when primary metric drop > 5% absolute or sustained regression for 3 hours. Pager on-call Applied ML.
  2) quality-regression-warning (SEV3): triggered when drop between 2-5% for 24h. Notify Applied ML Slack channel and create triage ticket.
  3) harness-failure (SEV2): harness job fails > 3 consecutive runs. Escalate to SRE.

Regression Triage Playbook (24h SLA):
1) Triage and classify (0-2h):
   - Owner acknowledges alert and records initial issue in triage template.
   - Classify as: A) Data-drift / prompt changes, B) Model change (weights, tokenizer), C) Serving config change (quantization/kernel), D) External infra issue.

2) Reproduce (2-6h):
   - Re-run failing eval-harness job pinned to the alerting window. Use --replay-window and include seeded RNG.
   - Compare outputs: baseline (previous stable model) vs current. Produce diff summary and representative failing prompts (top 10).

3) Root-cause and mitigations (6-18h):
   - If quantization-related: validate by switching to fp16 baseline and re-evaluating. If confirmed, revert quantization profile and notify runtime to hotfix.
   - If prompt-set/intent drift: update prompt sets, notify product owners, and consider temporary rollback.
   - If external infra: open SRE incident and follow incident runbook.

4) Postmortem and Follow-up (within 72h):
   - Create an incident summary in confluence/incidents and update the model card with mitigation notes.
   - If regression indicates model-quality degradation, schedule retraining/onboarding review.

Operational Config and Example Files:
- Example eval config (YAML):

  # eval-harness/tests/gptx-small/config.yaml
  model_name: "gptx-small"
  version: "2026-11-01"
  weights_uri: "s3://redwood-models/gptx-small/v1"
  tokenizer: "gptx-tokenizer"
  sequence_length: 1024
  batch_size: 8
  quant_profiles: ["int8-default", "q4_variant_a"]

- Example prompt-set entry (JSONL):
  {"id":"summ-0001","input":"Summarize: The quarterly earnings report shows ...","reference":"Net revenue increased 12% year-over-year.","tags":["summarization","finance"],"expected_metric":"rouge-l>=0.55"}

Tooling and Automation:
- repos: eval-harness (tests, runners, adapters), quantization-profiles (catalog + test vectors).
- CI: all onboarding PRs must pass: unit tests, eval-harness smoke run, quantization regression-lite run.
- Dashboards: eval-quality-overview (per-model, per-intent), quantization-impact matrix.

Decision Gates (must pass to proceed to canary):
- Functional tests: 100% pass on smoke suite.
- Quality gate: primary metric within acceptance thresholds.
- Security/safety review: no regressions on guardrail prompt sets (safety metrics unchanged).
- Performance gate: meets latency and cost improvement targets for selected profile.

Playbook Examples and Templates (links)
- Model Intake template: /confluence/templates/model-intake
- Triage template: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/triage-template
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

Frequently encountered failure modes and recommended responses:
- Failure: increase in hallucination rate after quantization. Response: revert profile, rerun with per-layer calibration, consider mixed-precision fallback.
- Failure: P95 latency spike on Hosted. Response: verify kernel selection and batch sizing; scale Dedicated pool if capacity-related.
- Failure: eval-harness job flaky on CI. Response: pin RNG seeds, add retry wrappers, and open CI reliability task.

Appendix: Quick CLI snippets
- Run a single eval-harness job locally:
  $ python -m eval_harness.run --config tests/gptx-small/config.yaml --output results/gptx-small-v1.json

- Compare outputs and produce diff summary:
  $ python -m eval_harness.tools.compare --baseline results/gptx-small-baseline.json --candidate results/gptx-small-v1.json --top-k 10 --report report.html
